# Opbox's MODEL SURFACE, as verb ids, vendored into boltrig.
#
# What the Opbox MCP door actually publishes, which is the set a mapping pack
# can name. Distinct from opbox-model-surface.txt, which is TABLE names for a
# different gate ([2026] VJS-COUNTY 8 D9's domain-model boundary).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. boltrig/capabilities/packs/opbox.yaml maps operation ids to
# canonical capabilities, and apply_mapping_pack SKIPS an id the door does not
# expose - deliberately, because a pack outlives the catalogue it maps and a
# stale entry should bind nothing rather than mint a binding onto an operation
# that is not there. The cost of that choice is that an Opbox RENAME silently
# unmaps a capability: no error, no log, the canonical verb simply stops being
# offered. This list is what turns that silence into a failing check.
#
# Vendored rather than read live: opbox is a separate private repository and the
# door needs a bearer, so a gate that depends on reaching a running deployment
# is a gate that passes only on one machine. Same pattern, and same reasoning,
# as opbox-model-surface.txt and .vjs/canon-citations.txt.
#
# A STALE LIST IS CONSERVATIVE. It can miss a NEW opbox verb (which maps nothing
# and is caught the moment someone tries to map it), never invent one.
#
# Refresh deliberately, from a live door:
#   select id from verbs where id like 'opbox.%' order by id
#
# Captured 2026-08-19 from the Classical Visas deployment: 443 verbs.
